EQUIPMENT REQUIRED
In this lesson, you will learn about the operation of AC motors and generators.
INTRODUCTIONM
Generators and electric motors perform opposite functions.
Motors convert an electrical input to a mechanical output..
Generators convert a mechanical input to an electrical output.
Using a motor to supply the mechanical input to a generator is one way that generators are driven.
Motors drive components to produce motion and generators supply power that is not normally available.
AC motors and AC generators are types of rotating machinery.
As an electronic technician, you will be required to service equipment that uses AC motors and generators.

There are, however, some major differences between the DC and AC motor construction.
AC motor rotors do not have turns of wire connected externally to a voltage source through a commutator assembly.
AC rotors (inductor type) have a distinct appearance and are often referred to as squirrel cage rotors.
The squirrel cage rotor is simpler and less expensive to manufacture than the DC rotor.
The squirrel cage rotor requires no commutator or brush assembly. This reduces cost, maintenance and sparking.

Rotor current depends on the relative motion between the stator's magnetic field and the conductor (rotor).
If the rotor is locked (no rotation), there is maximum relative motion between the rotating stator field and the conductor (rotor).
This produces maximum current and maximum torque.
If the rotor is turning at the same RPM as the stator's magnetic field, there is no relative motion between the rotating stator field and conductor (rotor).
No current is produced and the torque is zero.

Generators change mechanical energy to electrical energy. They do this by operating on the principles of magnetism.
DISCUSSION
The first principle of magnetism used in generators is: like magnetic poles repel and unlike magnetic poles attract.
When two magnetic poles of the same potential are close together, the magnetic fields repel the magnets.
When two magnetic poles of opposite potential are close together, the magnetic fields attract the magnets.
The second principle of magnetism used in generators is: when a conductor passes through a magnetic field, electric current is produced.
When the conductor moves up through the magnetic field, current flow is produced.
When the conductor moves down through the magnetic field, opposite current flow is produced.
As long as these two principles are remembered, generator action is simple.

Now let's discuss the Revolving-Field generator............
In the revolving-field AC generator, DC from a separate source is passed through field windings on the rotor via the slip rings and brushes.
This arrangement provides for a rotating field of fixed polarity.
This magnetic field extends outward from the ends of the rotor, sweeping across the armature windings of the stator.
As the rotor turns, alternating voltages are induced in the armature windings, first of one polarity and then the other.
The north and south poles of the rotor's magnetic field alternately cut across each armature winding.
The AC output is taken from the stationary armature windings.
There are no sliding contacts in the output circuitry to spark or arc-over. This feature allows high-voltage and high-power applications for revolving-field generators.
The DC exciter voltages seldom exceed 250 VDC, minimizing the need for bulky rotor field coils and insulation. Revolving-field generators can produce very high output voltages.

A single-phase alternator physically resembles a single-phase AC motor.
The stator coils are connected in series, so the induced voltages in each coil are together and in phase.
The output voltage is four times the voltage of any one winding and exhibits a single-phase sine-wave output wave form.

In order to understand many of the terms used in three-phase power distribution systems, you must first know how the alternator windings are connected.
These are two popular winding configurations used for alternator armatures.
Three-phase systems are usually Wye connected.
The term "Wye" is derived from the shape of the connection.
One lead of each armature winding is connected together to a common or neutral line, which is usually grounded.
The other three leads are called "Phase Voltages", labeled A, B and C.
Since each phase has a common ground (neutral), any one phase can be used to power single-phase loads.
Most high power transmission lines are three-phase Wye connected.
Your home appliances run on single-phase AC................
LINE VOLTAGE is the voltage between any two phases: A to B, B to C, and C to A.
There is a simple conversion between line voltages and phase voltage.
The line and phase current of a Wye connected generator are equal to each other.
The second type of three-phase power connection is called the "Delta" connection.
The Delta connection has no neutral and uses three wires only.
For a Delta connection, one end of two armature coils are connected together and the output is taken across any one phase.
In a Delta connection the line and phase voltage are equal. The difference is in the line phase and current phase. To find the line current use the conversion factor 1.73 x Phase Current..
In most cases, the Wye connected transformers are used. So this is where the majority of our discussion will be focused.

Let's discuss the loads on a Wye connected generator.......
Most Wye connected systems utilize balanced Wye connected loads.
Balanced means the resistor values are the same. This implies the voltage across each phase resistor is equal.
Since current is determined by phase voltage and resistance, line current will equal phase current. Any difference results in neutral current.
A balanced load represents a safe circuit.

1. All generators, in fact all rotating machinery, operate on the same principle: Magnetism.
2. There are two fundamental types of AC generators, Revolving- armature and Revolving-field..

3. In a Revolving-field generator, DC from a separate source is passed through the field windings on the rotor via the slip rings and brushes. However, slip rings and brushes are not in the output circuitry, this design prevents arc-over.
4. Single-phase, two-phase, and three-phase alternators are available. Three-phase is the most common, due to the low- cost, flexibility, and efficiency compared to DC generators of the same rating.
5. Three-phase alternators may be connected in either a Wye or Delta configuration..'
6. In the Wye configuration, the line CURRENT is equal to the phase CURRENT, where in a Delta configuration, the line VOLTAGE is equal to the phase VOLTAGE.
7. Balanced Wye systems, where line current equals phase current, will have neutral current if there is any difference in phase current. This makes a balanced load a safe circuit.
